implementation_statement: Before 2026 only Finance's 2023 WISP contained access rules. POL-02 (P06) applies to the whole group and was approved 2026-09-25; access procedures (joiner, mover, leaver, access review) are due 2026-11-30.

Accounts are created in the identity provider from HR onboarding requests and federated to the ERP, HRIS, loan servicing, and distribution systems. Gaps: subsidiary terminations reach IT by email about 3 business days late; SYS-11 uses local accounts outside SSO, and 4 former technicians were still active there (P07); no periodic access review; no break-glass accounts.
evidence: IdP user export; termination sample of 8; SYS-11 user list

implementation_statement: Each SaaS system enforces role-based access; roles are assigned by the process owner (Controller for ERP, HR Director for HRIS, Finance President for loan servicing). Cloud tenant access uses provider IAM roles for 3 named administrators.
evidence: ERP role matrix; servicing system role report; cloud IAM export

implementation_statement: ERP separates vendor master changes from payment release, and the bank enforces dual approval for wires and ACH. Gap: vendor bank-detail changes are accepted by email without independent verification (P01 R-002).
evidence: ERP SoD report; bank dual-control settings

implementation_statement: Standard users have no local administrator rights on managed endpoints. Gaps: 3 of 41 collaboration sites granted all-employee access, including Finance's loan archive (fixed 2026-08-13 for the archive); all Finance users can bulk-export from the servicing system.

7 standing global administrator accounts exist, including 2 MSP accounts. Plan: 2 standing administrators plus 2 break-glass accounts; MSP elevation time-limited and approved per task. Due 2026-11-30.
Accounts lock for 15 minutes after 10 failed sign-ins; the provider's smart lockout blocks password spraying.
Endpoints lock after 15 minutes idle through device management; tablets lock after 5 minutes.

Remote access to SaaS uses SSO with MFA; administrative access to the cloud tenant uses the VPN plus MFA. Gap: no conditional access blocks unmanaged personal devices, and MSP remote tools are not restricted by source address.
evidence: Conditional access report; MSP tool settings

implementation_statement: All laptops and tablets are enrolled in device management with encryption, PIN, and remote wipe.

No rules existed for sharing across subsidiaries or with outside parties. POL-04 now sets sharing rules by classification; sensitivity labels and blocking of anonymous links on Restricted sites are due 2026-10-31.
Training is covered by POL-05 (approved 2026-09-25); a training procedure and calendar are due 2026-11-30.
Annual online security awareness training for all employees since 2025 (57 of 60 completed in 2026). Gaps: no phishing simulations; content not updated for AI assistant use or payment fraud.
No social engineering training. Planned: payment-fraud and help-desk impersonation module for payables, treasury, HR, and help desk staff; quarterly phishing simulations. Due 2026-11-30.
IT staff attend vendor training. The Qualified Individual has no documented security training plan (16 CFR 314.4(e)(3)-(4)). Plan: annual training budget and record for the 3 IT staff.
evidence: Certificates on file for 2 of 3 IT staff

implementation_statement: Providers generate sign-in, admin, mailbox, file, and cloud control-plane events by default. Gap: events to be logged are not defined in writing, and mailbox auditing for non-owner access is off for 9 mailboxes.
Provider audit records include user, time, source address, action, and result.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: No review of audit records today. Planned: weekly review of sign-in risk, admin activity, and mailbox rule changes; monthly review of servicing system access reports by the Finance President. Due 2026-12-31.
Identity and email audit logs are kept only 30 days under the current license. Planned: log workspace with 1-year retention. Due 2026-12-31.
Audit record generation is enabled on all SaaS systems and the cloud control plane.
First independent control assessment performed 2026-09-08 to 2026-09-11 (P07). Plan: annual assessment each September.
POA&M maintained in P07 with owners and dates; reviewed monthly by the CFO.
No continuous monitoring strategy. Planned with the log workspace and 24x7 managed detection and response; metrics reported to the Board of Managers twice a year. Due 2027-01-31.
Endpoint baselines are enforced through device management. Gap: no documented baseline for firewalls, the identity tenant, or cloud workloads.

No change management process or change log for identity, network, cloud, or integration changes. Planned: change log with standard, normal, and emergency changes approved by the IT Manager or CFO. Due 2026-12-31.
Security settings enforced on endpoints and some tenant settings (legacy authentication blocked). Gaps: tenant-wide sharing defaults and cloud network rules not reviewed against a standard.
Endpoints run only approved software; application control blocks unsigned installers; unused cloud ports are closed.
Endpoint inventory is automatic in device management. Gaps: no inventory of SaaS applications, service accounts, or network devices across subsidiaries.
Contingency expectations are in POL-01 and POL-04; a group contingency plan procedure is due 2026-12-31.
No written contingency plan. The BIA (P05) was completed 2026-09-25 and sets recovery priorities; the plan is due 2026-12-31.
No backup restore or contingency plan tests have ever been run. Planned: quarterly restore tests; annual tabletop. First restore test 2026-10-30.

provider_if_inherited: Cloud provider backup service; SaaS vendors
implementation_statement: Daily backups of the 4 cloud tenant workloads with 30-day retention. Gaps: backups share the production account, region, and administrator roles; email and files have no independent backup.
No documented recovery procedures for the cloud workloads. Planned with the contingency plan, due 2026-12-31.
All employees and MSP staff have unique accounts in the identity provider. Gaps: SYS-11 local accounts; a shared generic account on 3 Supply counter desktops (P07).

MFA (push with number matching) is required for all administrator accounts. The 2 MSP administrator accounts were excluded from the MFA policy until 2026-09-12 (P07 finding, corrected). Gap: not phishing-resistant; hardware security keys planned for administrators by 2026-11-30.
MFA is required for all users on every SSO application and the VPN. Hardware keys for finance, treasury, HR, and Finance staff are planned (P01 R-001).

Passwords are at least 12 characters and checked against a banned list. Gaps: no identity check before MFA resets; the Supply counter account password has not changed since 2024; SYS-11 has its own weaker password rules.
POL-03 (approved 2026-09-25) sets group incident response rules; procedures are in the P08 runbook.
The P08 runbook for shared-platform compromise was approved 2026-09-25. Gaps: no 24x7 detection; no forensic retainer; not yet tested.
Staff report incidents to the IT help line. Gaps: subsidiary staff did not know the reporting line (5 of 12 interviewed); no documented regulatory reporting path until P08.
POL-03 and the P08 runbook together form the group incident response plan, approved 2026-09-25. Gap: plan not yet distributed to subsidiary Presidents or tested.
Retired drives are wiped with a verified tool or destroyed by a vendor that issues certificates.
The HQ network closet is badge-controlled; the Supply and Home Services network cabinets are locked with keys held by the site President and IT.
POL-01 to POL-05 were approved by the CEO on 2026-09-25 and apply to all four entities.
This SSP (version 1.0, 2026-09-25) documents the shared platform. It must be updated after any acquisition or major change.
POL-05 rules of behavior, including AI assistant rules, approved 2026-09-25. Signed acknowledgments due from all 60 employees by 2026-10-31.
The group security program is documented in POL-01 and this SSP. Finance's WISP will be replaced by POL-01 to POL-05 plus a Finance supplement by 2026-12-31.
The IT Manager leads the group program and is the written Qualified Individual for Finance; the Finance President oversees the Qualified Individual (16 CFR 314.4(a)(2)).
Risk tolerance and acceptance authority are defined in POL-01 and P01. Gap: not yet applied consistently at subsidiaries, and the Board of Managers received its first cyber report on 2026-09-25.
Background checks at hire for all employees; credit checks for Finance, treasury, and payables roles.
HR emails IT when employees leave. Gap: average 3 business days to disable for subsidiary staff; same-day target set by POL-02.
POL-01 requires an annual SP 800-30 risk assessment for the group, which also meets 16 CFR 314.4(b).
Group risk assessment completed 2026-08-28 (P01). Finance's previous written risk assessment dated from 2023.
No vulnerability scanning or penetration testing. Planned: monthly authenticated scans of endpoints, firewalls, and cloud workloads; annual penetration test. First scan due 2026-11-30.
New SaaS purchases are approved by the CFO. Gap: no security requirements or questionnaire in purchasing; the AI assistant was bought without a security review.

Contracts with the ERP, HRIS, and loan servicing vendors include confidentiality terms; SOC 2 reports are on file and the ERP report was reviewed on 2026-09-18 (P09). Gaps: HRIS and loan servicing reports not reviewed; MSP contract has no security terms; no service provider inventory.
Firewalls at all three sites; cloud network rules allow SFTP only from the bank's addresses and admin access only over VPN. Gap: Home Services firewall firmware two major versions behind.
All SaaS and SFTP traffic uses TLS 1.2 or later; site-to-site VPN uses IPsec; email to the bank and carrier uses enforced TLS.
Providers use FIPS-validated or industry-standard encryption for data at rest and in transit per their SOC 2 system descriptions.

Full-disk encryption on all laptops and desktops; provider encryption at rest for SaaS and cloud storage. Gap: ACH files on the SFTP server use only provider-default keys, and any IT administrator can read them.
Endpoints patch automatically; the MSP patches cloud VMs monthly. Gap: Home Services firewall firmware out of date; no tracking of SaaS vendor advisories.
EDR on all laptops and desktops; email attachment and link scanning in the productivity suite.
EDR and identity risk detections alert the IT team. Gap: alerts are watched only in business hours; no network egress monitoring; no alerting on mass file access.
evidence: EDR alert log; IdP risk report

implementation_statement: No automated integrity checks on subsidiary data feeds into the ERP; the Controller reconciles monthly by hand. Planned: daily record-count and total reconciliation. Due 2027-03-31.

No group retention schedule. ACH files are kept indefinitely. Planned: retention schedule in POL-04, 90-day deletion of ACH files, and a disposal procedure for Finance customer information. Due 2026-11-30.

Only the ERP vendor review (2026-09-18) has been performed. Planned: annual review of critical suppliers (ERP, identity, suite, cloud, HRIS, loan servicing, MSP) using SOC 2 reports and a questionnaire (P09).
